subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should the Slack follow-up be limited to latency-aware docs/setup guidance for HTTP Request URLs, or should OpenClaw change Slack setup/default behavior beyond the existing `mode: "http"` support?
rationale: HTTP mode already exists and official Slack docs prefer HTTP for deployed apps when Socket Mode is not required, but changing setup or defaults would alter operator expectations and deployment requirements.

options.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
options.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default and update Slack docs/setup guidance to prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

options.title: Change setup or defaults
options.body: Have maintainers sponsor a stronger setup/default change that steers new hosted Slack installs toward HTTP mode with explicit upgrade and operator guidance.

options.title: Accept current guidance
options.body: Decide the existing transport table is sufficient and close only after recording that no latency-specific guidance or setup change is planned.

recommendation.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
recommendation.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default and update Slack docs/setup guidance to prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the measurement, landed the partial Slack fixes, and explicitly scoped the remaining HTTP guidance decision.
